name: regime_library_v1
plan: docs/EVOLUTION.md, phase 5, the regime library (the owner, 14 Nov 2026: "market may not behave the same way 2 months later, 3 months later, a year later. How our trading desk is going to evolve in that process?"); and the deferred test of the forgetting record (docs/prereg/evolution_probation_v1.json, not_registered_A_forgetting: "revisited in phase 5, where replays over years of history give it the long, stale records it needs, and a test that can pass")
question: S: when the desk meets a market, does what each kind of structure did in the most SIMILAR past markets (by the fingerprint) choose better than what it did on AVERAGE? A: does a record that FORGETS (weights halving every 60 sessions) choose better than the cumulative one? Both are asked on the same replay of the desk's structures through every session of real option closes the warehouse holds, walk-forward (each session's choice uses only what was known at its close), and both are answered as one number: R a trade gained or lost against choosing by the cumulative record
not_for: nothing here trades, sizes or moves a limit (2.5% a trade, 5% a day, 10% drawdown; the convexity book's 0.5% a trade and 3% a month), and nothing changes in AUTO v2 because of this spec. The replay is research on end-of-day closing prices (evidence class real_eod_approximation, as docs/prereg/expiry_wings_v1.json): it is NOT evidence that any structure is profitable, qualifies nothing for paper money, and is never a paper-gate or profitability claim. What a PASS allows is set in use_if_passed and needs the owner

dataset.fingerprints: NIFTY's daily closes from the daily-history dataset of 2026-11-08 (release daily-history, 2026-11-08_daily_YYYY.parquet; NIFTY content hash 5002ba113391e894a2207f0c, source Yahoo, 2013-01-02 to 2026-11-06; status unverified only for 8 missing days of 3411, all before 2019-01-02, cross-checked 60 of 60 against the warehouse 2019-2026). The same series the brief's fingerprint is computed from each morning (premarket/tailrisk.py, Yahoo), so the library describes the past exactly as the desk describes today. Each session's fingerprint is quantdesk/premarket/fingerprint.compute(asof = that session), from closes up to its close and nothing after; 3,026 sessions, 2014-07-16 to 2026-11-06 (the first 378 closes are its warm-up). Every session after 2026-11-06 is computed the same way from the same source
dataset.options: the warehouse's fo_bhav (release warehouse, fo_bhav_YYYY-MM.parquet), NSE's F&O bhavcopy: every NIFTY and BANKNIFTY option, daily close, settlement price, contracts traded; months 2019-01 to 2026-11 (November only for 2026-11-02, the exit of the lock's entries). The run records the SHA-256 of every file it reads
dataset.spot: the warehouse's nse_index_close (NSE's official closing value, the price index options settle on): NIFTY 50 and NIFTY BANK
dataset.pool_start: 2019-01-01: the first session with real option closes. Only sessions from it have replay outcomes
dataset.window: test sessions: every session from the first whose embargoed pool (library.embargo) holds at least 250 sessions, counted on the fingerprint calendar (by the 2026-11-06 fingerprints, 2020-04-15; 1,626 sessions to 2026-11-06, a few fewer to the lock) through 2026-10-30, the lock. The outcome of a session needs the next session's close, so the last outcome read is 2026-11-02's
dataset.not_backfilled: the warehouse holds no option closes before 2019. The 2008 crash, the 2013 taper and the 2016 demonetisation are not in this replay: the fingerprint library reaches them (the aeron7 index minutes, 2007 to Feb 2023, external_verified, allowed use regime_research), the options do not. A backfill of fo_bhav to 2008 (NSE's old-format bhavcopy is archived from 2000) is a new dataset and, if it is wanted, a new spec (regime_library_v2), never added to this one

what_was_seen_before_registering: the builder computed the 3,026 fingerprints from closes and read their features' distribution, their correlations and the kernel's n_eff at five bandwidths (docs/prereg/sims/regime_library_v1/library_features.out.txt), and read the column names of one fo_bhav month and one nse_index_close year. No replay outcome, no option price series and no forward return was computed or looked at. Earlier desk studies did read fo_bhav 2019 onwards: the expiry studies (expiry_seller_v1 to v4, expiry_eve_law_v1 and v2, expiry_wings_v1) sold premium entered 1 to 10 sessions before expiry and held to settlement. This replay's protocol (entered at every close, held one session) was never run, but its short-premium families overlap those results near expiry: the builder knew, before registering, that selling premium into the last sessions before an expiry did not survive costs in those studies

library.why_these: the fingerprint's NIFTY-only features: every one exists at every session since 2014. The stocks' correlation and dispersion and the cross-asset percentiles are left out (their series start later or carry survivorship); the brief-only features (US VIX, the dollar, US yields, events) have no history in the desk's data
library.scale: each feature as a robust z against the pool (the median and 1.4826 x the median absolute deviation of the pool's sessions, the pool being the past only), clipped to +/-4
library.distance: the root mean square of the six z differences
library.embargo: the pool of session d is the sessions from pool_start to d - 61 (at least 60 sessions before d): the library is about markets LIKE today's in the past, not the last few weeks, which the live record already holds. Without the embargo, the nearest fingerprints are yesterday's, and similarity would be recency by another name
library.why_h_0.5: fixed from the features alone (library_features.out.txt): on the test sessions, h 0.5 leaves n_eff (the kernel's effective number of sessions, (sum w)^2 / sum w^2) at 115 / 286 / 713 at its 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles, under 30 in 3% of sessions; h 0.35 leaves it under 30 in 10%, h 0.25 in 39%. In the simulation (power, below) h 0.35 and 0.5 have the same power to within the simulation's error, and 0.5 the steadier n_eff

replay.family_definition: a family is a structure of quantdesk/paper/auto2.py STRUCTURES (its family in Lab.fit's hierarchical model), its legs from the same table, placed by the same function (auto2.legs_for over the strikes listed that day for that expiry, at-the-money = the listed strike nearest the official close), at each of its registered widths. Its outcome in a session is the mean R of its widths that could be traded that session; with none, the family has no outcome that session
replay.left_out: calendars and diagonals (CAL, PCAL, DGC, DGP: their worst case values a later expiry at its floor, which closing prices do not price cleanly), the Convexity desk's structures (convex payoffs under their own caps and exits; probation leaves them out for the same reason), futures (direction only), and invented structures (they change over time). All are in the shadow book as before
replay.entry: at each session's close: the nearest expiry after that session (an option expiring at this close is not entered), every leg at its closing price worsened by research.warehouse_research.leg_cost (a tick plus a half-spread of at least a tick, 0.2% of premium): bought above the close, sold below it. Every leg must have traded that session (contracts > 0, close > 0) and be priced at least auto2.MIN_PREMIUM; else that width is not traded
replay.exit: at the next session's close, every leg at its close worsened the same way; a leg that did not trade then is valued at NSE's settlement price for that day, worsened the same way, and counted. If the expiry is that next session, the legs settle at their intrinsic value on the official index close, with no exit spread, and STT on the intrinsic value of exercised long legs (warehouse_research.STT_EXERCISE)
replay.costs: the desk's statutory fee model as AUTO v2 pays it today (paperlink/cli.auto_v2: execution.costs.CostModel on the desk's config, one lot of today's lot size, entry and exit), for every session in the window: the question is how structures behave in kinds of market, not what costs were in 2019, and charging today's costs keeps the 2024 STT and lot changes out of the comparison. A width whose round-trip costs exceed auto2.MAX_FEES_R of its risk is not traded, as AUTO v2 refuses it
replay.R: the outcome in R as AUTO v2 scores a shadow trade: the profit or loss per unit after spreads, fees and STT, over the risk (the structure's worst loss at expiry from auto2.payoff_bounds at the entry fills, plus the round trip's fees), clamped to -5 .. +10 as Lab.add clamps it
replay.why_one_session: closing prices can replay an entry at a close and an exit at the next close and nothing finer: AUTO v2's take-profits, stops and intraday exits happen between closes and cannot be replayed honestly. Overnight is what the desk's overnight strategies carry
replay.no_view: the replay has no market read and no news model (neither has a history), so every family trades every session it can, whatever the direction. The tests compare families WITHIN a direction group, which is how the desk uses a family: given a view, which structure

choosers.FLAT: the cumulative record: for each underlying and family, the mean R of all its outcomes from pool_start to d - 1 (the outcome of session d - 1 is known at d's close)
choosers.SIM: the library: the kernel-weighted mean R over the embargoed pool (w as in library), shrunk to FLAT: (n_eff x kernel mean + 30 x FLAT) / (n_eff + 30), n_eff counted over the sessions where the family has an outcome
choosers.EW: the record that forgets: the mean R with weights halving every 60 sessions, over pool_start to d - 1
choosers.choice: in each of the six cells (two underlyings x three groups), each chooser takes the family with the highest estimate among those with an outcome that session; FLAT's choice is the reference. A family with no outcome in the pool yet is not chosen

tests.statistic: D(d) = the mean over the cells of y(the chooser's family) - y(FLAT's family), in R; a cell where they choose the same family adds 0; a cell with fewer than two families with outcomes is left out of that session's mean, and a session with no cell left has no D
tests.inference: the mean of D over the test sessions; Newey-West t with 20 lags (research.edges.hac_mean); and, as a check that the choices' persistence is not overstating it, with 60 lags
tests.pass: a test PASSES when its t is at least 1.96 with 20 lags AND with 60 lags (one-sided 2.5% each: two tests, Bonferroni), and its choice differs from FLAT's in at least 10% of the cell-sessions
tests.fail: any other result is a FAIL of that test, reported with its mean, both t, its 95% interval and the share of cell-sessions where the choices differed. A choice that differs in under 10% of cell-sessions is reported as NOT INFORMATIVE, not as a FAIL
tests.one_run: each test runs once, on the window to the lock. No bandwidth, embargo, shrinkage, feature, family list or cost is changed after a result is seen; a change is a new spec on data this run did not touch

power.evidence: docs/prereg/sims/regime_library_v1/power.py (numpy, seed 5, 200 worlds each), output power.out.txt: the REAL fingerprint path and kernel weights of the 1,626 test sessions, SYNTHETIC outcomes for 16 families on 2 underlyings (an overnight move scaled by each session's real 20-session volatility, priced in, so that a volatile market alone pays neither long nor short volatility; per-family loadings on it; normal noise of 0.2 R; a regime effect of size delta, each family's own smooth function of the six features; optionally a random-walk drift per family that no feature describes, and heavy tails with rare multi-R payoffs)
power.results_h_0.5: the share of worlds that PASS by the registered rule (t >= 1.96 at 20 and at 60 lags, choices differing in at least 10% of cell-sessions). S: nothing differs 0.035; fixed family means 0.010; drift only 0.005; heavy tails 0.005; regime 0.03 R 0.385; regime 0.05 R 0.815; regime 0.08 R 0.995; regime 0.05 R with heavy tails 0.740; regime 0.05 R with drift 0.230. A: nothing differs 0.025; fixed family means 0.005; heavy tails 0.000; drift only 0.650; regime 0.05 R 0.325; regime 0.08 R 0.835; regime 0.05 R with drift 0.730. At h 0.35 S passes 0.830 of the regime 0.05 R worlds and 0.025 of the nothing-differs ones; at h 0.7, 0.730 and 0.030
power.reading: S has about 80% power when the best structure's edge moves by 0.05 R a trade (sd over sessions) with the kind of market (74% with heavy tails), under 40% at 0.03 R. Its false PASS rate was 3.5% where nothing differs (nominal 2.5%; with 200 worlds that is within about one standard error) and 1% or less in every other null world, including one where the family means drift and only a forgetting record could follow. A PASSES where change is drift (as it should) and seldom where only the market's kind matters. Drift of the simulated size (0.15 R over the sample) cuts S's power to about 0.23: a FAIL of S is therefore not proof that kinds of market do not matter, only that the library could not show it on this sample. A noisier chooser loses to the cumulative record when the families' means simply differ and stay put (mean D -0.0014 R for S, -0.0029 R for A): that is the price a PASS has to overcome

reported_descriptively: never a claim and never a second test: (1) SIM against EW, the same statistic; (2) D by calendar year and by named windows (2020-04 to 2020-12, the recovery; 2022, the rate hikes; 2024-06-03 to 2024-06-14, the election result; 2024-11-20 onwards, the F&O rule changes and BANKNIFTY's weekly expiry ending); (3) the share of sessions each regime key of phase 1 covers in the window (by 2026-11-06's fingerprints, 'normal/down' held on 8 of 3,026 sessions and 'high/up' on 14: the key is lopsided, which phase 3's choice by regime must allow for, and which the continuous features used here do not suffer from); (4) the replay's coverage: sessions, families and widths traded, legs valued at settlement

code.module: quantdesk/research/regime_library.py (the library, the replay and the tests), run by the Study workflow (a new choice, regime-library), merged after this spec. The run summary and the logs carry only what publication makes public; per-family output goes where publication says, and in the app (if S passes) over the keyed relay, never in the public site. The fingerprints are fingerprint.compute; the legs, the bounds and the clamp are auto2's own functions, imported, never copied
code.rule: the report records the git commit of the run and this spec's SHA-256; a change to any definition or parameter above after this spec is merged is a new spec (regime_library_v2)

forward_rule: the sessions after the lock are untouched. 120 sessions after the lock (about May 2027), both tests are run again on those sessions only, by the same code, and reported beside the first result; they confirm or weaken it and change no verdict
publication: as docs/prereg/evolution_probation_v1.json decided on the owner's delegation (the owner's Claude Code session of 14 Nov 2026, claude.ai/code/session_011DBceCbQNtu6df3GhXrgYD: "Up to you how you feel it's right to do, so do it in that way."): the verdicts and aggregates (each test's mean D, t, interval and share of differing choices; the descriptive items' aggregates) go to this public repository (docs/prereg/results) with this spec's SHA-256; which family did best in which kind of market, per family and per regime, is a trading result and stays private: on the relay only, or in an expiring workflow artifact only if AES-256 encrypted the way recorded Kite market data leaves a runner (docs/AUTONOMY.md); never in a run summary, a log, an unencrypted artifact, a release, the gh-pages site or this repository, which are all public
lock: this file is never edited once it is merged

use_if_passed.S: a PASS allows the phase 5 code to compute, each morning, every family's library estimate for today (SIM, from the replay to the last close) and to show it in the app beside the family's own record. Using it as the family prior in Lab.fit (the mean a family's members are shrunk towards, now 0) changes which strategies AUTO v2 chooses for paper money and can loosen a choice, so it is the owner's decision with this result in front of them (docs/RENAISSANCE.md, invariant 7). The builder's recommendation, if S passes: run it in shadow first (record what the prior would have chosen beside what was chosen) for 60 sessions
use_if_passed.A: a PASS is the evidence the deferred forgetting record lacked. Adding it to Lab changes choices for paper money: the owner's decision, with the probation spec's own simulation (it chose worse under Thompson draws in most worlds) beside this result
use_if_passed.neither: nothing in AUTO v2 changes. The library itself (the fingerprints of every past session) still serves phase 4 (breaks and the unfamiliar-market guard, which only tighten) and the app's Market regime panel

owner_decisions: this spec is research and changes nothing that trades. The owner merges it, as the plan's phases are the owner's. Everything a PASS could change in AUTO v2 is the owner's to approve afterwards (use_if_passed)
